subject: Startups
title: How Dilution Works
description: Learn How Dilution Works in one minute.

hook.text: You own 50% of your startup. After Series A, you own 35%. After Series B, 22%. Your slice shrank—but the pie grew.

buildup.text: Dilution happens when new shares are issued to investors.

discovery.text: A founder with 20% of a $1 billion company owns $200M. That's often more valuable than 80% of a $10M company.

climax.text: The goal is smart dilution: give up equity that buys growth exceeding the dilution.

punchline.text: Dilution is fine if each round makes your smaller slice worth more.

quiz.question: What happens to a founder's ownership percentage after each funding round?
